chunks: Yahya ibn 'Imran from Harun ibn Kharijah from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the statement of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic:
And We gave him his household and the like of them with them

I said, 'His children, how was he given the like of them with them?' He said: 'He revived for him from his children who had died before that by their natural lifespans, the like of those who perished on that day.'

key_terms.بِآجَالِهِمْ: By their natural lifespans / fixed terms
key_terms.مِثْلَهُمْ: The like of them / equal number

ai.seo_question: How did Prophet Ayyub receive 'the like of his family' according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (as), the concept of 'like of them' (mithlahum) in Surah Al-Anbiya is interpreted through the lens of resurrection and divine recompense. The Imam clarifies that Allah restored Ayyub’s deceased children by reviving them according to their natural lifespans, while simultaneously granting him an equal number of new offspring who perished on the same day, illustrating a precise divine accounting of loss and restoration.

en.hubeali: H 14802 – Yahya Bin Umraan, from Haroun Bin Kharjat, from Abu Baseer, who has narrated the following:
Abu Abdullahasws regarding the Statement of Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic:
“[21:84] and We gave him his household (that he had lost) and the like thereof along with them”.

I said, ‘His (Prophet Ayub<sup>as</sup>) children, how was he<sup>as</sup> given the like of them, with them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He<sup>azwj</sup> Revived for him<sup>as</sup> from his<sup>as</sup> children who had died before that of natural causes, and the like (number) of those who had died on that day’.

and We gave him his household (that he had lost) and the like thereof along with them”.

I said, ‘His (Prophet Ayub (as)) children, how was he (as) given the like of them, with them?’ He (a.s.) said: ‘He (azwj) Revived for him (as) from his (as) children who had died before that of natural causes, and the like (number) of those who had died on that day’.
